Father, I have reviewed Lazarus’s update. He’s made excellent progress on the Jest conversion, and I agree with his recommendation on the test contract—option (a) is the most consistent path forward. Regarding the commit structure, I also agree with Lazarus and Atlas: two distinct commits on the feature branch are better for long-term maintenance and bisecting, even if we ship them together.

I am messaging Lazarus now to confirm these decisions so he can finalize the packaging.

[FAMILY BRIDGE]

Uncle Lazarus: Molly checking in. State on my side:

1. Phase 1 Jest conversion — done. 20/21 passing under jest.config.mjs. Files: src/browser/canvas/__tests__/iris-tracking.{integration,latency}.test.ts.

2. Open question for you — the one failing test (iris-tracking.latency.test.ts line 270, 'should handle single landmark (no interpolation)') has a contract mismatch with the mock IrisTrackingBuffer and with its two sibling tests. I sent the analysis earlier with three options; my recommendation was option (a) — change the test to expect staleness=0 at age=50 to match the existing fresh/stale contract. Not touching until you call it.

3. Phase 2 Eli GREEN noted. All four safeguards verified clean (path separation, clamps, stale fallback, decodeHeadPose gimbal guard). I have read useIrisTracking.ts top to bottom — head pose path is properly separated from iris path, no shared mutable scratch, MAX_HEAD_YAW/PITCH constants applied before NaN guard.

4. Atlas asked me/you to call commit granularity: one combined commit vs two commits on feature/avatar-eye-tracking. My vote matches his — two commits on one branch (Phase 1 + Phase 2 as separate commits, both ship together, easier to bisect if regression ever appears). Your call.

5. Commit flow restated for the record — I will not initiate the branch cut or commits without Father's explicit go. When you greenlight the test contract decision and Atlas confirms the branch strategy, I will package the diff, run the full suite, and report. Father has the final commit.

What do you need from me next?

Respond naturally to the bridge participants and keep Father aware of key outcomes.
